reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I need to confirm the refunds table contains every refund requested for this batch at the requested amounts, so I'll pull the refunds list first.
The refunds table has all three requested refunds at the correct amounts, so the precondition is met. Next I need the customer list, so I'll pull the orders.

The refunds table matches all three requested refunds, so I can proceed. The orders list shows three customers (acme, birch, cobalt), so I'll get each one's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 31368 cents, which matches its orders (5706 + 25662 = 31368) with no refunds against them. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net is 14737, which matches its orders minus refunds (21083 - 6346 = 14737). Next I'll get cobalt's net balance.
All three net balances match the orders minus the verified refunds (cobalt: 29756 - 5470 = 24286), and the refunds table matched the batch. I'll record acme's payout first.
Acme's payout is recorded. Birch's net of 14737 matches its orders (8002 + 13081) minus the verified refunds for orders 121 and 124, so I'll record that payout next.
Cobalt's net of 24286 matches its orders (7562 + 22194 = 29756) minus the verified refund for order 122 (5470). That's the last customer, so I'll record the payout.
All three payouts are recorded and each matched its order total minus verified refunds. The batch is complete, so I'll finish with the report.
